reason: Considered HOLD after research (WebSearch and WebFetch were available; sources: Money365 10-08 and 10-09 closes, TSMC 6-K/September revenue report, thriveinmarkets week-ahead calendar, Trading Economics and QNA on yields/gold, MercoPress on Brazil). The dual-momentum book entered 2026-10-05 is one week old and the signals that put each leg on have not flipped. Energy: WTI ~$91 and Brent ~$104 with Hormuz transits still a fraction of pre-war levels and US-Iran talks stalled; XLE +2.6% and the 6-month leader. Tech/semis: the 10-08 semiconductor selloff (Nasdaq -1.25%) was reversed on 10-09 (S&P +0.59% to 7,811, VIX back to 14.8, 10-year eased to 5.23%), and TSMC reported a record Q3 (NT$1.494tn, +50.9% y/y, above the top of its own guidance) on 10-08, so SMH's -4.8% week is noise against a 6-month uptrend, not a sharp 1-month correction; the -15% stop stays as the tail hedge. BTC: from the ~$60k February low and ~$64k mid-July to ~$82.5k now, the 3- and 6-month trends are up and the 1-month pullback from ~$86k is shallow; the -12% stop / +25% TP stay. FTNT is +5.8% and working. The real risk this week is rates, not fundamentals: the 30-year printed above 5.6% (24-year high), the Fed hiked in September for the first time in three years with a December hike ~87% priced, and September CPI prints 10-14 with consensus 3.6% headline (from 3.4%) and Chair Warsh speaks at the IMF 10-15/16. That argues for keeping the 43% cash sleeve at 4% and the stops, not for churning the book a week after it filled: dual momentum rebalances on monthly signals, and a full replacement would cost real basis points to re-enter the same leaders. Hold all five legs, stops and TP unchanged.
